headline_findings: [verified] The shipped health schema `fitforge.health.v1` is not the prewalk's compact per-day record (sl/eff/st/rhr/hrv/wtd/ae): it is per-metric arrays of `DailyMetricPoint {date, value, unit}` for restingHeartRate/hrvSdnn/bodyMass/bodyFatPercentage/steps/activeEnergy plus hkUuid-keyed `HealthSample` rows for sleep and workouts, and there is no wrist-temperature, sleep-stage, efficiency or SpO2 field anywhere in code (apps/web/lib/native/forgeBridge.ts:40-83; apps/web/lib/health/store.ts:69-76).

[verified] The readiness engine consumes only sleep hours (manual, else observed), soreness/energy/stress 1-5, an `unwell` boolean, `rhrDeltaBpm` (deducts 11 at >= +5 bpm) and `hrvDeltaPct` (deducts 8 at <= -20 %); baselines are trailing medians that need >= 14 RHR days and >= 30 HRV days, and temperature plays no role at all (apps/web/lib/readiness/engine.ts:73-98,126-151; apps/web/lib/health/selectors.ts:22-23,40-48).

[verified] A logged set is just `{reps, weight_kg}` inside a `WorkoutSession {id, dayId, dayName, finishedAt, exercises[]}` stored newest-first as one mutable JSON document under `fitforge.workoutlog.v1`, capped at 200 sessions; there is no per-set timestamp, RPE, provenance or append/event log, and the normalizer silently strips any extra field on load (apps/web/components/features/shared/workoutLog.ts:21-49,102,106-116,326-331).

[verified] `apps/ios` is a hand-rolled SwiftUI WKWebView shell with zero package dependencies (XcodeGen spec, HealthKit engine, native storage mirror, ForgeBridge v1); Capacitor was only evaluated in the prewalk and never installed, and README.md:379-382 is stale in calling apps/ios an untouched MVP scaffold (apps/ios/project.yml:1-92; apps/ios/README.md:3-19; git commit 0f48c99; zero `@capacitor` entries in package-lock.json).

[verified] ForgeBridge v1 is a 9-message, additive-only JSON envelope contract (`{v:1, id, type, payload}`) with runtime guards on the web side, a Codable mirror in Swift and 12 frozen fixtures round-tripped by both test suites, so a BLE band slots in as a new capability string plus new `device/*` message types and fixtures, not as a new transport (apps/web/lib/native/forgeBridge.ts:142-163,203-225,442-473; apps/ios/FitForge/Bridge/ForgeBridge.swift:12,111-131; fixtures/forgebridge/README.md).

[verified] The workout player always knows the current exercise, the active set index and that set's `SetTarget {reps, repsLow, repsHigh, loadPct, rpe, role}`, and confirms a set through a `CollarLatch` button that also starts the row-sized rest timer, so plan-aware rep detection can be fed from state the player already computes every render (apps/web/components/features/workout/WorkoutPlayer.tsx:578-602,749-761,1131-1137; packages/shared/src/rules/progression.ts:245-268,719-733).

[verified] Cloud sync is one Firestore document per user, whole-bundle last-write-wins with a 900 KB client cap and a 950 KiB rules cap, and the prefixes `fitforge.health.`, `fitforge.cycle.`, `fitforge.readiness.` and `fitforge.activeSession.` never ride it while still riding the deliberate file export; any new device key holding health-adjacent data must be added to that denylist (apps/web/lib/demo/store.ts:1058-1066,1116-1132; apps/web/lib/auth/sync.ts:62,178-180,331; firestore.rules:38-44).

[estimate] The 180-day retention bound (warn at 150) exists because of that 900 KB ceiling; measured from the shipped shapes a 6-exercise x 4-set session serialises to about 2.1 KB, so 180 days at four sessions a week is roughly 210 KB and the 200-session cap about 410 KB, meaning per-set device timestamps fit comfortably but per-rep IMU streams must never enter the synced log (apps/web/lib/demo/retention.ts:30-32; sizes computed with node from workoutLog.ts shapes).

[verified] The health/AI boundary is real in code: the adapt request carries only `sleepHours, soreness, energy, stress, unwell`; RHR/HRV deltas never leave the device, although an Apple-Health-prefilled sleep chip does reach the worker as a coarse `sleepHours` (apps/web/lib/readiness/context.ts:39,71-79; apps/web/components/features/today/MorningCheckIn.tsx:104-113; workers/coach/src/index.ts:1285-1340).

[verified] The static-export, no-server architecture blocks nothing a band needs on-device: `public/` is copied verbatim into `out/` so firmware images can be hosted as static files on Pages, but any vendor-cloud OAuth (Whoop/Fitbit/Garmin style) needs the Cloudflare worker, which today verifies Firebase ID tokens and CORS-allow-lists origins but has no KV binding and no per-uid rate limiting (apps/web/next.config.mjs:10; .github/workflows/pages.yml:84-89; workers/coach/wrangler.toml:19-21; workers/coach/src/index.ts:2011-2016).

[verified repo facts, secondary platform claim] On the primary target the band link cannot be Web Bluetooth: the shell locks a WKWebView to goforge.fit (app-bound domains) and WKWebView/iOS Safari expose no `navigator.bluetooth`, so iPhone needs a CoreBluetooth engine in the shell speaking ForgeBridge, and a browser Web Bluetooth adapter only serves Android/desktop Chromium (apps/ios/FitForge/App/RootView.swift:26-27; apps/ios/project.yml:50-51).

[estimate] A minimal end-to-end integration is roughly 2,000-2,800 new lines (about 1,100-1,500 TypeScript, 500-700 Swift, 5-7 fixtures) touching about 10 existing files and 12-15 existing test files; the 24/7 health half is nearly free if the band writes HR/HRV/sleep to Apple Health (the existing HealthKit engine ingests it), so only the set-detection half needs the direct BLE link (sized against forgeBridge.ts 478 lines, HealthKitEngine.swift 596 lines, AppleHealthCard.tsx 163 lines).

detailed_notes:
# FitForge codebase lens: what a band integration touches

Read at HEAD 542f932 (`Stop scrolling a page that has not mounted yet`); no file was modified. Line numbers are from this checkout.

## 0. Orientation and two stale docs

- The product is a Next.js static export (`apps/web/next.config.mjs:10`, `output: 'export'`). State lives in localStorage behind `apps/web/lib/demo/store.ts` (1,742 lines) plus separate slices for the workout log, the in-progress session, health and readiness. The only off-device pieces are optional Firebase sync (`apps/web/lib/auth/sync.ts`) and one Cloudflare worker (`workers/coach/src/index.ts`, 2,195 lines).
- `apps/ios` is NOT Capacitor and NOT the archived Supabase MVP that README.md:379-382 describes. Commit 0f48c99 (`The iOS shell: Apple Health feeds the forge`) replaced it with a SwiftUI/WKWebView shell with zero SPM dependencies (`apps/ios/project.yml:1-92`, `apps/ios/README.md:3-19`): `App/RootView.swift` (WKWebView of https://goforge.fit, app-bound domains), `Bridge/ForgeBridge.swift` and `ForgeBridgeMessages.swift`, `Health/HealthKitEngine.swift` (596 lines), `Storage/StorageMirror.swift`, `Views/ConsentView.swift`, `Views/HealthStatusView.swift`, with `DecodingTests.swift` and `StorageMirrorTests.swift`. `.github/workflows/ios.yml` generates the project with XcodeGen and builds/tests it on macos-15. Capacitor is mentioned only in `docs/PREWALK-IOS-HEALTH.md`; `package-lock.json` has zero `@capacitor` entries.
- Test surface today: 22 unit-test files under `apps/web/lib` (`tsx --test`), 53 Playwright specs with 258 `test(` calls, 116 shared-rule tests, worker tests and the Swift tests. README (100 e2e) and PRODUCT.md (205) are both behind.

## 1. The logged set / session model

Key `fitforge.workoutlog.v1` (`apps/web/components/features/shared/workoutLog.ts:21`). Shape (lines 23-49):
- `LoggedSet { reps: number; weight_kg: number }` and nothing else: no timestamp, RPE, duration or provenance.
- `LoggedExercise { exercise_id, exercise_slug, exercise_name, mechanics, primary_muscles[], secondary_muscles[], sets[] }`, muscles snapshotted at log time (ADR 0004).
- `WorkoutSession { id, dayId, dayName, finishedAt (ISO), exercises[] }`; `LogState { version: 1, sessions[] }` newest first.
- `logSession` (326-331) prepends and slices to `MAX_SESSIONS = 200` (line 102). Ids are `sess-${Date.now()}` (`WorkoutPlayer.tsx:694`). `finishWorkout` (671-725) keeps only `done` sets and never writes warm-ups.
- It is a MUTABLE DOCUMENT, not an append log: each write rewrites the whole blob through `safeSetItem`, and a cross-tab `storage` listener drops the cache (294-301). `normalizeSet` (106-116) rebuilds every set as `{reps, weight_kg}` only, so any additive device field (timestamp, confidence, `source: 'device'`) is silently discarded on the next load unless the normalizer is extended; `validateWorkoutLog` (232-239) rejects imports that needed repair.
- In-progress state is `fitforge.activeSession.v1` (`apps/web/lib/workout/activeSession.ts:35`): `ActiveSetSnapshot { reps, weight_kg, rpe, done }`, exercises keyed by `rowId` (the `RoutineExercise.id`), `exerciseIndex`, `startedAt`, a 12 h TTL (line 42) and restore gated on `dayId` (170-173). The rest timer is not persisted.
- Where a device-generated set is inserted: live, into `WorkoutPlayer` state through `updateSet`/`completeSet` (`WorkoutPlayer.tsx:550-602`), which the save effect (484-504) mirrors into the active session; unattended, as a whole `WorkoutSession` via `logSession`, which needs a `dayId` plus the exercise snapshot fields, so the matcher must resolve an exercise id from motion classes before anything can be logged.
- Budget: `RETENTION_DAYS = 180`, `WARN_AFTER_DAYS = 150` (`apps/web/lib/demo/retention.ts:30-32`), driven by the cloud document limit (`MAX_BYTES = 900_000` at `sync.ts:62`; `bundle.size() < 950 KiB` at `firestore.rules:42`). Measured from the shapes: one set is 25 B, a 6x4 session about 2.1 KB, 180 days at four sessions a week about 209 KB, the 200-session cap about 406 KB. Timestamps per set add roughly 10 KB per 180 days; per-rep IMU or timing streams must stay on the band or in a non-synced key.
- Clobber risk: sync is whole-bundle last-write-wins (`sync.ts:14-25`, `setDoc` at 331). A device that pushed before pulls with `merge` (`sync.ts:526`) and `mergeSessions` unions by id (`store.ts:1238-1242`), so device sessions survive if ids are unique. The archived Supabase `set_logs` row (`packages/shared/src/types/database.ts:603-637`: set_number, rpe, is_warmup, completed_at, exercise_name_snapshot) is a ready-made richer shape if `LoggedSet` is ever versioned.

## 2. Health aggregates and the readiness engine

What shipped differs from the prewalk sketch (`docs/PREWALK-IOS-HEALTH.md:44-48`, sl/eff/st/rhr/hrv/wtd/ae):
- Key `fitforge.health.v1` (`apps/web/lib/health/store.ts:40`). `HealthState { version: 1, daily: Partial<Record<QuantityMetric, DailyMetricPoint[]>>, samples: Partial<Record<'sleep' | 'workouts', HealthSample[]>>, meta }` (69-76); `meta` carries the per-metric permission map, sync stamps, `disconnected` and `healthWeightDates`.
- Metrics (`forgeBridge.ts:40-56`): `sleep`, `restingHeartRate`, `hrvSdnn`, `bodyMass`, `bodyFatPercentage`, `steps`, `activeEnergy`, `workouts`. Quantities cross as `DailyMetricPoint { date: 'YYYY-MM-DD' (the user's local day), value, unit }` with units `count/min`, `ms`, `count`, `kcal`, `%`, `kg` (`HealthKitEngine.swift:78-94`). Sleep and workouts cross as `HealthSample { hkUuid, start, end (ISO with local offset), value, unit ('hr' | 'min'), kind ('asleep' | HKWorkoutActivityType name), kcal? }`.
- There is no wrist temperature, sleep stage, efficiency, SpO2 or respiratory rate anywhere; the contract killed VO2max, respiratory rate and stage scores for v1 (`docs/IOS-SHELL-CONTRACT.md:76-79`).
- Ingestion `ingestBatch` (267-288) replaces by (metric, date) or by `hkUuid`, sorts and bounds to `MAX_DAYS = 400` and `MAX_SAMPLES = 1600`; body mass also writes through `logWeight` with manual-wins provenance (241-260). `highWaterMarks()` (296-314) feeds `health/requestSync.haveUpTo`; null means backfill (90 days native, `HealthKitEngine.swift:315`).
- Readiness inputs (`apps/web/lib/readiness/engine.ts:20-52`): `sleepHours | null`, `soreness/energy/stress` 1..5, `unwell`, and optional `observedSleepHours`, `rhrDeltaBpm`, `hrvDeltaPct`, `externalWorkoutYesterday`. Deductions (73-98): sleep under 5.5 h = 30, under 7 h = 12; soreness 5 = 25, 4 = 14; energy 1 = 25, 2 = 14; stress 5 = 18, 4 = 10; RHR delta >= +5 bpm = 11; HRV delta <= -20 % = 8. Score = 100 minus the sum; >= 70 green/proceed, >= 45 yellow (technique if soreness >= 4, else reduce), otherwise red/rest; `unwell` short-circuits to rest with `safety: true` (100-110).
- Baselines (`apps/web/lib/health/selectors.ts:22-23, 40-63, 92-115`): RHR is the trailing 14-day median (min 14 points, excluding the judged morning), HRV the trailing 30-day median (min 30 points), `hrvPct = (today - baseline) / baseline`. `overnight(date)` returns null without an `asleep` sample ending that morning. `MorningCheckIn.tsx:95-152` assembles the `CheckIn`: observed sleep pre-selects the nearest of five chips and stays overridable; `rhrDeltaBpm = rhr - rhrBaseline` only when both exist.
- So a band must produce, at minimum, one `restingHeartRate` point per local day (bpm), one `hrvSdnn` point per day (SDNN ms), `asleep` sleep samples with local-offset ISO timestamps and a stable per-session uuid, and optionally `steps`, `activeEnergy` and `workouts`. The engine stays silent on RHR for 14 days and on HRV for 30. Temperature and SpO2 would be schema extensions with no consumer today.

## 3. The native bridge and where BLE slots in

- Source of truth `apps/web/lib/native/forgeBridge.ts` (478 lines). Envelope `{ v: 1, id: uuid, type, payload }` (158-163). Types (144-154): page to native `bridge/hello`, `health/requestPermissions`, `health/requestSync`, `health/ackBatch`; native to page `bridge/helloAck { shellVersion, bridgeVersion, capabilities[] }`, `health/permissions`, `health/batch`, `health/syncComplete`, `bridge/unsupported`. Transport: page to native `window.webkit.messageHandlers.forgebridge.postMessage` (291-301); native to page `window.ForgeShell._receive` (330-344). Detection is the injected global, never the user agent (286-288). Per-type guards (203-225), an `onBridgeMessage` registry (310-322), `initForgeBridge` (442-473) with a 3 s `helloAck` timeout, and `useShell()` exposing `inShell`, `capabilities`, `shellVersion` (`useShell.ts:34-51`), mounted at the root by `ShellBridgeDriver.tsx` (`app/layout.tsx:185`).
- Swift side: `ForgeBridge.swift` owns two `WKScriptMessageHandler` channels (`forgebridge`, `storageMirror`), the documentStart restore/shell-global/storage-shim scripts (153-257) and dispatches `.hello/.requestPermissions/.requestSync/.ackBatch` (111-131); capabilities are the literal `['health', 'storageMirror', 'backupExport']` (line 12). `ForgeBridgeMessages.swift` decodes unknown types to `.unrecognized`. `HealthKitEngine` adopts `BridgeOutput { isReady, send(_:) }` (lines 5-9) and runs an ack-gated batch queue (152-259).
- Contract discipline: 12 fixtures in `fixtures/forgebridge/` are round-tripped by `forgeBridge.test.ts` (expected-type map 35-48, `>= 12` assertion at 51, exact capabilities assertion at 99) and by `DecodingTests.swift`; `shell-bridge.spec.ts:51-67` fakes the shell by planting `window.ForgeShell` and `webkit.messageHandlers.forgebridge` before boot.
- Slotting in a band: add a `device` capability; page to native `device/scan`, `device/connect {id}`, `device/forget`, `device/context {exerciseId, pattern, targetReps, restSeconds}`; native to page `device/status {connected, battery, firmware, lastSeen}`, `device/setEvent {eventId, at, reps, durationMs, confidence, exerciseGuess?}`; and reuse `health/batch` unchanged for band-derived RHR/HRV/sleep (the guards accept any `HealthMetric`). On iOS that is a `Device/BleEngine.swift` (CoreBluetooth central) adopting `BridgeOutput` exactly as `HealthKitEngine` does, plus `NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription` and `UIBackgroundModes: [bluetooth-central]` in `project.yml`'s `info.properties`. In a plain browser, Web Bluetooth works only in Chromium on Android/desktop, not in iOS Safari or WKWebView, so the browser adapter is a secondary path. The cheapest health half: if the band's own app writes HR/HRV/sleep into Apple Health, the existing engine ingests it with zero new code and only set detection needs the direct link.

## 4. The workout player state machine

`apps/web/components/features/workout/WorkoutPlayer.tsx` (2,252 lines):
- State: `exercises: ExerciseState[]` (routine row, exerciseId/Name after swaps, `sets: SetEntry[] {reps, weight_kg, rpe, done}`, `warmups: boolean[]`, `warmupAck`, `patternAlreadyWarm`) at 109-137; pager `index`, `rest {endsAt, total} | null`, `finished`, `startedAt` (325-350). Built by `buildInitialState` (254-286) from `dayPrescriptions` (`lib/demo/prescription.ts:123-171`).
- Every render computes `current = exercises[index]`, `plan = prescriptionFor(...)` and `activeSetIdx = current.sets.findIndex(s => !s.done)` (519, 749-761). `plan.sets[i]` is a `SetTarget { index, reps, repsLow, repsHigh, loadPct, rpe, role: 'top' | 'work' | 'backoff', cue }` (`packages/shared/src/rules/progression.ts:245-268`); `suggestedLoadKg(topSetKg, loadPct)` resolves kilos. The player therefore knows current exercise, target reps and suggested load at all times; the payload for plan-aware rep detection already exists in memory.
- Confirmation: reps/weight/RPE are `<input type=number>` via `SetField` (`SetField.tsx:148-212`, aria-labels `Set N reps` etc.); done is the `CollarLatch` button `Mark set N done` (`WorkoutPlayer.tsx:1131-1137`) calling `completeSet(i)` (578-602), which toggles `done`, fires `haptic('confirm')` and starts the rest timer sized by `restSecondsForSet(row.rest_seconds, role, mechanics)` (top sets x1.25, `progression.ts:719-733`). `RestTimer` (1815-1937) is a deadline-derived overlay with +/-15 s, skip and `navigator.vibrate(120)`; it dims but never disables the pager. Editing set 1's weight re-derives back-off loads (550-576); `addSet` (626-660), `onSwap` (662-669); warm-ups are separate booleans (608-624). `finishWorkout` (671-725) is idempotent via a ref, logs `done` sets and clears the active session.
- A device hook fits as `applyDeviceSet(reps, ...)` aimed at `activeSetIdx`: prefill reps and either auto-latch on high confidence or leave the latch to the athlete (the readiness product law 'never silent' argues for confirm-first). The `sessionDirty` save effect persists it; a band indicator belongs in the header row beside the set counter (791-813) without touching the `workout-set-counter` and `set-row-N` testids.

## 5. Sync and privacy rules that constrain a device

- `SYNC_DENYLIST_PREFIXES` (`store.ts:1058-1066`): `fitforge.health.`, `fitforge.cycle.`, `fitforge.readiness.`, `fitforge.activeSession.`, excluded by `readExtras(forSync)` (1116-1132) from `exportAllState({forSync: true})` (1139-1150), which `bundleForCloud()` uses (`sync.ts:178-180`); still included in the deliberate file export because that action is the consent (`syncDenylist.test.ts:32-60`, `cloud-restore.spec.ts:249`). `DEVICE_LOCAL_PREFIXES` (`fitforge.cloudPushed`, 1081) are excluded from every copy. Extras are capped at 32 keys of 512 KiB (1044-1045).
- Contract laws (`docs/IOS-SHELL-CONTRACT.md:17-35`): health data only under `fitforge.health.*` / `fitforge.cycle.*`, no health data through the worker, no mirror uploads, no verdicts from single readings, and the engine's shape is fixed (optional observed fields only).
- Consent gates: a native priming screen leads to one `requestAuthorization` (`ConsentView.swift`, `HealthKitEngine.swift:115-131`); `health/permissions` reports `yieldedData` as the only honest per-metric signal; web-side `disconnect()/reconnect()` stops ingesting but keeps data (`store.ts:345-356`); `AppleHealthCard.tsx` renders only in-shell. Erase removes every `fitforge.*` key plus Cache API entries (`store.ts:1463-1491`) and deletes the Firestore document first when signed in (`sync.ts:395-435`, `SettingsView.tsx:516-530`).
- AI boundary: the adapt request sends only `sleepHours, soreness, energy, stress, unwell` (`context.ts:39,71-79`; the worker parses exactly those, `index.ts:1285-1340`); RHR/HRV deltas never leave the device, though a Health-prefilled sleep chip travels as a coarse `sleepHours`.
- A Devices surface therefore needs pairing (scan/connect/forget) via the transport, status (connected, battery, firmware, last sync), per-stream toggles (HR/HRV/sleep into `fitforge.health.v1`, set detection into the workout log), an auto-log versus confirm-first preference, an OTA action, and its own key. Pairing state should be device-local; any buffered band health data must live under `fitforge.health.` (Law 2) or a new prefix added to the denylist, with `syncDenylist.test.ts` and `cloud-restore.spec.ts:170-275` extended.

## 6. Minimal integration plan

New modules (sized against analogous files):
- `apps/web/lib/device/protocol.ts`, payload types and guards (150-200 LOC).
- `apps/web/lib/device/transport.ts`, `DeviceTransport` interface, status store and `useDevice()` modeled on `ShellStatus` (120-180).
- `apps/web/lib/device/bleShell.ts`, ForgeBridge adapter over `onBridgeMessage`/`sendToShell` (120-180).
- `apps/web/lib/device/bleWeb.ts`, Web Bluetooth adapter for Android/desktop Chromium (200-300).
- `apps/web/lib/device/setEvents.ts`, event buffer, matcher to `activeSetIdx`, unattended-session builder (200-250).
- `apps/web/lib/device/store.ts`, `fitforge.device.v1` with normalize/repair per the house invariant (150-200).
- `apps/web/lib/device/ota.ts` plus `apps/web/public/firmware/manifest.json` (100-150).

- Bridge: `forgeBridge.ts` +80-120, `ForgeBridgeMessages.swift` +80, `ForgeBridge.swift` +40, `apps/ios/FitForge/Device/BleEngine.swift` 400-600, `project.yml` +6, 5-7 fixtures.

Tests to update: `forgeBridge.test.ts` (EXPECTED_TYPE map, fixture count, the exact capabilities assertion at line 99), `syncDenylist.test.ts`, `importModes.test.ts`, and `store.test.ts`/`selectors.test.ts`/`engine.test.ts` only if metrics are added; e2e `shell-bridge.spec.ts` (helloAck fixture), `health.spec.ts`, `workout.spec.ts`, `set-form.spec.ts` (label walk), `prescription-fidelity.spec.ts` (viewport position of set 1), `workout-resume.spec.ts`, `portability.spec.ts`, `cloud-restore.spec.ts`, `settings.spec.ts`/`profile.spec.ts`, `screenshots.spec.ts`, `touch-targets.spec.ts`; Swift `DecodingTests` picks up new fixtures automatically.

Architecture check: the static export blocks nothing on-device. `public/` is copied verbatim into `out/` (`pages.yml:84-89`), so firmware images and a manifest can be static files on Pages, and the in-shell service worker only caches `/_next/static/**` (`public/sw.js:11-14`), so firmware fetches are never stale. What the static site cannot do is hold a client secret: any vendor-cloud OAuth must go through `workers/coach`, which already verifies Firebase ID tokens (`index.ts:2011-2016`) and CORS-allow-lists origins (`wrangler.toml:33`) but has no KV binding for token storage (`wrangler.toml:19-21`) and no per-uid rate limiting, and Law 2 forbids health payloads through it, so it may broker tokens only. Background 24/7 collection on iPhone needs either the `bluetooth-central` background mode in the shell or a band that buffers and dumps on connect, which maps directly onto the existing `requestSync/haveUpTo`, `batch`, `ackBatch` flow.
open_questions: Does the owner want wrist-temperature and SpO2 in v1 at all, given the shipped readiness engine has no consumer for them and adding metrics is a bridge-version event (new HEALTH_METRICS entries, store/selector/engine changes, new fixtures)?
Should band-detected sets auto-commit (latch closed) or be offered for one-tap confirmation, in keeping with the readiness product law that nothing is applied silently?
Where do unattended sessions (phone closed, band alone) land: a synthetic `dayId` such as 'device', or matched to the scheduled routine day by time and movement pattern?

Will the band's companion path write HR/HRV/sleep into Apple Health (making the health half free through the existing HealthKit engine) or speak only BLE to FitForge, which then needs the shell to run CoreBluetooth in the background?
Is Android in scope? The only browser-side BLE path is Web Bluetooth in Chromium, and there is no Android shell in the repo.
Is it acceptable to publish firmware images publicly at goforge.fit/firmware/* on GitHub Pages, and what signing/verification does the band expect before flashing?
Should `fitforge.device.*` be treated as device-local (never copied, like `fitforge.cloudPushed`) or merely sync-denylisted (copied in file exports)?
Per-set device fields: extend `LoggedSet` additively (touching the strict normalizer and import validation) or keep a sidecar key such as `fitforge.device.sets.v1`?

If a vendor-cloud (Whoop-style) integration is ever wanted, will the worker gain a KV binding and per-uid rate limiting first, and how does token brokering stay within contract Law 2 (no health data through the worker)?
Should README.md:379-382 (apps/ios described as an untouched MVP scaffold) and the e2e test counts in README/PRODUCT.md be corrected as part of this work?
How should the 200-session cap and the 180-day retention interact with a band that may auto-log many short sessions per week?
Which BLE GATT profile does the band expose: standard Heart Rate Service plus a custom set-event characteristic, or a fully custom service? This decides whether `bleWeb.ts` can reuse standard UUIDs.
